objective: Proof. Assemble the classification of the five three-place knots on plain and signed cubic systems (failures possible, recognisable, decision complexity, what the failing systems make easy) from tickets A and B, MUTUAL-SELECTION-20261031-001 and KNOT-COUPLING-20261031-001, and prove: assuming P != NP, not-all-equal is the only non-affine three-place knot whose failing cubic systems form a non-empty class recognisable in polynomial time, and the only three-place knot with mutual selection (its failing systems make the knot's law and the dimer law easy, both #P-hard on general systems).
status: Proved by PINNING-20261031-001C-P001: assuming P != NP, among all 34 three-place knot relations (five classes) only not-all-equal is mutually selecting on cubic systems (failures non-empty and recognisable, own count #P-hard in general): parity is affine, the clause never fails, the Fibonacci law and x or (y != z) pin and their failures are coNP-complete; on plain systems unconditionally only not-all-equal fails; the knot's failures (Pfaffian signings) also make the dimer law easy; recognition test checked on all 1,380,864 signings with n <= 6
title: The knot is the only three-place law with mutual selection
